author: EmuCore - Hub
title: Diagnose a PS2 game that renders the HUD but not the world
summary: Use the surviving HUD as evidence that presentation is active, verify the disc image, reset draw-disabling overrides, compare hardware APIs and a short software reference, then capture the smallest reproducible world-geometry failure.
heroAlt: PCSX2 game capture from a renderer regression comparison with interface and world layers

blocks.text: Treat the visible HUD as a layer boundary

If counters, menus, or the game's HUD still draw, the output surface and at least part of the GS command stream are alive. The missing part may be world geometry, framebuffer composition, or a broad manual rule that discards draws. Before changing accuracy, record whether the world is black, transparent, frozen on an earlier frame, or replaced by a single flat color. Those symptoms lead to different tests.
Do not increase skip-draw values to make a corrupt layer disappear. A skip rule can remove the entire world while leaving 2D overlays, exactly reproducing this symptom.

items: A normal in-game save that reaches the affected scene without an emulator save state.
Verified serial, region, revision, and personal image hash.
Screenshots of current global and per-game graphics values.
System GPU driver with texture replacements and shaders disabled.
A short log showing renderer initialization and the transition into gameplay.
1. Cold-boot the title and confirm whether menus, FMV, and gameplay fail at different boundaries.
2. Reset skip-draw, manual hardware fixes, texture offsets, and inherited per-game patches for this serial.
3. Retest at native internal resolution on the original hardware API.
4. Close the session, select the other supported hardware API, and replay the same transition.
5. If both paths keep only the HUD, run the scene briefly in software rendering and capture whether world geometry returns.
6. When software is correct, return to hardware and test only a documented title-specific renderer or GS correction.
7. If software is also empty, re-verify the image and test a clean profile before assuming a graphics-only fault.
8. Capture logs and exact settings from the smallest run that reproduces the missing world.

blocks.text: HUD and world often use different draw paths. A correct software frame proves the game produced world commands and narrows the failure to hardware translation or host-driver behavior. Failure across clean hardware and software paths points back toward the image, patches, game progression, or a broader emulator regression. Resetting draw-disabling controls first prevents a self-created symptom from contaminating that decision.
The corrected profile must render more than a convenient still frame.

items: World geometry, characters, particles, and HUD appear in their intended order.
Menus and FMV still transition into gameplay without a black holdover frame.
Camera movement does not reveal large missing sectors.
A second area cold-boots with the same per-game setting.
The fix is attached only to the verified serial and revision.
Software and both hardware APIs fail on a verified image with clean settings: collect a regression report.
Only one custom driver fails: return to the system driver and report the driver package separately.
World returns when skip-draw is zero: retire the copied override.
The fault begins after a save-state load: reproduce from an in-game save before filing graphics evidence.

blocks.text: Rebuild the title profile from defaults

Remove the experimental profile, restore the recorded global renderer, select the system driver, and cold-boot at native resolution. Reapply only the one verified correction if it passed every area check; leave all discard-draw controls disabled unless official title-specific evidence requires them.
A black world is not always a black screen

Display range and OLED black level can crush dark scenery, but they cannot make geometry absent from a direct screenshot. Inspect a captured frame and renderer log before changing television or HDR settings.
Follow the PCSX2 general troubleshooting baseline
